title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 25-26). Let S = Spf of a formally smooth p-adic W-algebra, with a Frobenius lift F_S and closed fibre S_0. The category C consists of filtered F-crystals (M, ∇, F_M, Fil) that are extensions of constant pieces. The sub is Q'⊗_{Z_p}O_S, on which F is the identity (slope 0, unit-root/étale part). The quotient is P'⊗_{Z_p}O_S, on which F is p (slope 1, multiplicative part). P' and Q' are Z_p-lattices and T = Hom(P',Q') = P'^∨⊗Q'. This is exactly the Dieudonné-crystal situation of an ordinary p-divisible group (or ordinary abelian scheme) deforming over S.

Step 1. Choose an O_S-splitting φ: M ≅ P'⊗O_S ⊕ Q'⊗O_S. In coordinates (x,y):
- F_M(x,y) = (px, y + Φx) with Φ ∈ Γ(T⊗O_S);
- ∇ = d + N with N(x,y) = (0, ωx), where ω ∈ Γ(Ω̂^1_{S/W} ⊗ T⊗O_S).

Step 2. Another splitting differs by u(x,y) = (x, y + Lx) with L ∈ Γ(T⊗O_S). The gauge rules are F' = u F (F_S^*u)^{-1} and N' = uNu^{-1} − (du)u^{-1}. They give the boxed formulas
 Φ' = Φ + pL − F_S^*(L),  ω' = ω − dL.

Step 3. The conditions for (ω, Φ) to define an object of C:
(i) dω = 0, i.e. ∇ is integrable (flat).
(ii) F_S^*(ω) − pω = dΦ, i.e. F_M: F_S^*M → M is horizontal.
(iii) Φ_0 = 0, i.e. F_M respects the filtration over S_0, using a splitting adapted to Fil there, as noted at the end of p.25.

In modern terms, C (up to isomorphism of extensions) is classified by H^1 of a two-term double complex: the de Rham complex of T⊗O_S mapped to itself by (F_S^* − p), with a filtration/boundary condition. The cocycles are pairs (ω, Φ) satisfying (i)-(iii); the coboundaries are (dL, F_S^*L − pL). This is the complex computing Ext^1 in filtered F-crystals, i.e. a syntomic-type cohomology (the cone of p − φ on the filtered de Rham complex).

The evident continuation (p.27 is illegible) is to use the Poincaré lemma and Dwork-type integrality to gauge ω to 0. This makes Φ horizontal, hence constant up to the normalisation, and yields 'canonical coordinates', i.e. the Serre–Tate parameter through log q. That is the computation later done by Katz and by Deligne–Illusie (1981).
errors: Notational inconsistency carried from p.25: F_{M,φ} is written as the matrix (id Φ; 0 p·id) but defined as (x,y) ↦ (px, y+Φx), so the p sits on the other diagonal entry. The matrices for u, ∇ and F are written in an upper-triangular convention that does not match the formulas acting on (x,y). The boxed formulas themselves check out with the formula convention: F' = uF(F^*u)^{-1} gives Φ' = Φ + pL − F^*L, and the gauge transform gives ω' = ω − dL.
On p.25 Φ is said to lie in Γ(Ť⊗O_S), but with u(x,y) = (x, y+Lx) and F(x,y) = (px, y+Φx), Φ is a map P'→Q', i.e. it lies in T⊗O_S, the same space as L. Probably a slip.

The condition Φ_0 = 0 presupposes a splitting adapted to Fil on S_0 (as the marginal note on p.25 says). Correspondingly, L should be restricted to vanish on S_0 for the gauge action to preserve this normalisation. This restriction is not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Parametrising extensions of a slope-1 constant F-crystal by a slope-0 one via a splitting: Frobenius off-diagonal term Φ and connection form ω, with gauge rules Φ' = Φ + pL − F^*L and ω' = ω − dL
ideas.modern_name: Ext^1 of (filtered) F-crystals / Dieudonné crystal of an ordinary p-divisible group; local moduli of ordinary deformations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz, 'Serre–Tate local moduli' (1981); Deligne–Illusie, 'Cristaux ordinaires et coordonnées canoniques' (1981); Dwork for the underlying p-adic analysis
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in Grothendieck's 1970 Montréal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' and his 1970 ICM address; this explicit cocycle computation is not known there

ideas.what: Integrability dω = 0, horizontality of Frobenius F^*ω − pω = dΦ, and filtration condition Φ_0 = 0 as the cocycle conditions
ideas.modern_name: Cocycles in the cone of (φ − p) on the filtered de Rham complex: syntomic / Fontaine–Messing style cohomology computing Ext in filtered F-crystals (Fontaine–Laffaille-type categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine–Messing (1987), Kato; Fontaine–Laffaille (1982) for the categories

missed.claim: Around 1970 Grothendieck writes down, for extensions of constant F-crystals, the cocycle/coboundary description that amounts to H^1 of the mapping cone of (F^* − p) on the filtered de Rham complex. This is the computation underlying Serre–Tate canonical coordinates via crystals (Katz, Deligne–Illusie, 1981) and an elementary instance of later syntomic cohomology. It shows he was computing Ext groups of F-crystals concretely a decade before these works, though only the routine set-up survives here.
missed.quote: F_S^*(ω) − pω = dΦ ... exprime que F_M est compatible à la connexion
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's own crystalline approach to local moduli of ordinary objects, predating the published treatments. No new mathematics is present on the page.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is correct but standard by today's standards; it is the basic set-up for extensions of unit-root by slope-1 F-crystals. Its interest is historical: an early (c.1970) explicit appearance of the (F^* − p)-twisted de Rham cocycle conditions anticipating Katz/Deligne–Illusie and syntomic cohomology. The decisive continuation (canonical coordinates) is not legible.
transcription_corrections: 'que on a, si ω' = ω_{M,φ'}, que' is more likely 'qu'on a, si ω' = ω_{M,φ'}, que :' (on trouve).
Line 'Écrivons les conditions [-...-] sur Φ = Φ_{M,φ} et ω = ω_{M,φ} qui assurent qu'on a bien un objet de C. On a' seems right; the struck word before 'sur' looks like 'que doivent satisfaire'.
The right-margin boxed duplicate reads 'ω = ω_{M,φ} ∈ Γ(Ω̂^1_{S/W} ⊗ (T ⊗_{Z_p} O_S))', consistent with the main text (the image shows ⊗ with subscript q/Z_p).
